analysis.title: Marketcolour + Midterms Replay / Earnings
key_insights: US equities rallied after the midterms with lower oil and falling yields. SPX +158bps to 7688, NDX +91bps to 28,437, RTY +158bps to 2856. 8 of 11 sectors rose: Discretionary +5.09%, Communications +4.59%, Energy -4.75%.
The post-midterm backdrop favors owners of compute and hurts those who build out, sell into or power datacenters. Hyperscalers rose 3.5%, while neoclouds fell 7%, semis 2.5% and power 6%.
Rate-sensitive and lower-quality pockets outperformed. Homebuilders (GSXUBLDR Index) rose 714bps and low income discretionary (GSXULOWD Index) rose 487bps.
In Europe, Banks (SX7P) rose 4.3% and EU Renewables (GSXERNEW) rose 1.2%, while Defence (GSSBDEFE) fell 1.8%.

Historical stat: since 1952 the 12 months after a midterm have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the next 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6 and 12 month points in all 18 cases.

21 US baskets had a move larger than 3 sigma yesterday, the second highest count on a 1-year lookback (5 June was 25). The market is trading 'less data center, less defense budget, more homebuilding and more healthcare subsidies'.
Basket moves: ACA Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) +9%, Homebuilders (GSXUBLDR) +7%, Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) +4%, versus NeoClouds (GSXUNEOC) -8%, Power Up (GSENEPOW) -6% and Defense Spending (GSXUDFNS) -5%.

Rheinmetall: Q3 operating profit beat but FY26 sales and operating margin guidance was lowered. Revenue rose 32% to €3.15bn (3% below consensus). Operating profit rose 62% to €553mn (4% above consensus), a 17.5% margin. Free operating cash flow was -€82mn against consensus of +€123mn.

Legrand beat and raised. Organic growth was +19% vs consensus +11%, margins beat by 20bps, driving a 10% adjusted EBIT beat. OSG guidance was raised to 11-13% (consensus 10%) from 8-10%. Positioning in the name is 'clingy' and length was reduced further yesterday, so a small bounce is possible.

Maersk's initial read is weak against expectations. Q3 EBITDA was $4.7bn vs consensus $5.32bn, though FY26 EBITDA guidance was raised to $14-14.5bn from $10.5-12.5bn. Consensus was already $14.2bn and the buy side nearer $16bn+ (GSe $15.6bn).

Deutsche Telekom results were mixed. Group revenue and EBITDA AL beat, Germany service revenue was 0.4% ahead, and lower capex drove an OFCF beat. The buyback was lower and press reports suggest TMUS merger aspirations are not over. FY guidance was raised marginally for the US, and Germany EBITDA growth is now expected at the low end of the 2.5-3% FY26 guide.

IMCD's Q3 gross profit beat consensus by 2% (gross margin 50bps above), but EBITA was only in line. GS says the result is not good enough given the move lower in oil over 24 hours. FY26 organic EBITA growth outlook is called a somewhat meaningless statement given 9M growth of +4.6%. FCF rose 12% y/y.

Commerzbank missed and lowered NII guidance. Net profit was 1% below company consensus as NII (1% below) and other income undershot. CET1 was 14.2%, 0.2pp below consensus, hurt by FX, rate and credit spread effects on OCI and higher regulatory deductions.
Swiss Re's headline beat was supported by reserve releases and nat cat. P&C Re top line was a small miss against a lowered consensus: printed 4.5bn vs 4.88bn a month ago and 5bn in May.

Lanxess Q3 was in line. Guidance was narrowed to the upper end of the 450-500m range vs consensus about 490m, implying Q4 in line. Q3 was helped by a US tariff refund benefit and lower corporate costs. FCF was positive in Q3 and is guided positive in Q4.

market_movers.rationale: Conviction List Buy on Rheinmetall with 100% upside to the EUR2100 target. Q3 operating profit beat but FY26 sales and margin guidance was lowered.

sector_views.rationale: Homebuilders basket rose 7% on the market's tilt toward more homebuilding, with rate-sensitive pockets outperforming as yields declined.
ACA Beneficiaries basket rose 9% on the market's focus on more healthcare subsidies.
Neoclouds fell 7-8%, power 6% and semis 2.5% as the market priced less datacenter build-out.
Defense Spending basket fell 5% and European Defence fell 1.8% on the market's focus on a smaller defense budget.

earnings_insights: Rheinmetall Q3 (reported 11/5): revenue €3.15bn, +32% y/y, 3% below consensus. Operating profit €553mn, +62% y/y, 4% above consensus. Operating margin 17.5%. Order intake €2.89bn. Free operating cash flow -€82mn vs consensus +€123mn. FY26 sales and operating margin guidance lowered.

Legrand Q3 (reported): organic growth +19% vs consensus +11%. Margin beat by 20bps, adjusted EBIT 10% above consensus. OSG guidance raised to 11-13% (consensus 10%) from 8-10%. Margin guidance unchanged.
Maersk Q3 (reported): EBITDA $4.7bn vs consensus $5.32bn. FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to $14-14.5bn from $10.5-12.5bn (August guide), versus consensus $14.2bn, buy side $16bn+ and GSe $15.6bn.

Deutsche Telekom Q3 (reported): group revenue and EBITDA AL above expectations. Germany service revenue 0.4% ahead, Germany EBITDA a small miss. Lower capex drove an OFCF beat. FY guidance raised marginally for the US, non-US reiterated. Germany EBITDA growth now expected at the low end of the 2.5-3% FY26 guidance. Buyback lower.
IMCD Q3 (reported): gross profit 2% above consensus, gross margin 50bps above consensus, EBITA in line. FCF +12% y/y. 9M organic EBITA growth +4.6%.

Commerzbank Q3 (reported): net profit 1% below company consensus. NII 1% below, other income more negative than expected, operating and credit costs lower. CET1 14.2%, 0.2pp below consensus. NII guidance lowered.
Swiss Re (reported): headline beat supported by reserve release and nat cat. P&C Re top line printed 4.5bn vs consensus 4.88bn a month ago and 5bn in May.

Lanxess Q3 (reported): in line with consensus. FY guidance narrowed to upper end of the 450-500m range vs consensus about 490m, implying Q4 in line. Q3 helped by a US tariff refund benefit and lower corporate costs.
risk_factors: Lower oil is a headwind for Energy (-4.75%) and for oil-sensitive cyclical earnings such as IMCD.
Datacenter-related names (neoclouds, power, semis) face a lower-spending policy backdrop.
Rheinmetall's lowered FY26 sales and margin guidance and negative free operating cash flow.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning is described as light, with GS GBM Equities data as of 4 Nov 2026.
Legrand positioning has been 'clingy' relative to other electricals. Length was reduced across the space yesterday, so a small bounce is possible.
21 US baskets moved more than 3 sigma in one day, the second highest on a 1-year lookback (25 on 5 June).
geopolitical: US midterm election results drove a shift in expected policy toward less datacenter and defense spending and more homebuilding and healthcare subsidies.
The report notes a significant move lower in oil over the prior 24 hours alongside the post-midterm rally.
